headline: Medium risk: Khoj can ingest shared notes while Pipecat can route content to third-party LLM/STT/TTS services, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and Pipecat can expose text through shared-bus, stdin/stdout, or transport integrations, but no direct shared channel or parser bridge is documented. The plausible pathway is manual or integration-mediated content transfer, so injection risk exists but is not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF an operator copies Pipecat output into Khoj notes or prompts
IF a shared bus or file bridge is added between Pipecat and Khoj
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste workflow between the agents
Keep Pipecat and Khoj on separate workspaces
Add a human review step before importing Pipecat output into Khoj
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Pipecat touches conversation state, text, audio, video, and can call third-party LLM/STT/TTS services via allowlisted egress. If Khoj content is fed into Pipecat, sensitive notes can leave the local workspace through external APIs.
conditions: IF Khoj notes or indexed documents are passed into Pipecat services
IF Pipecat is configured with external STT/LLM/TTS providers
mitigations: Restrict Pipecat to local-only providers where possible
Do not route personal notes into Pipecat prompts
Review provider allowlists before enabling production traffic
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters on outbound text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access and no write or git privileges, while Pipecat exposes stdin/stdout and distributed shared-bus operation but no filesystem write capability is documented. Overlap is limited, so direct write contention is not evidenced.
conditions: IF Pipecat is extended with filesystem or git write plugins
IF both agents are mounted on the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep both agents off the same writable directory
Avoid adding write-capable plugins to Pipecat
Use separate service accounts and mounts
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes and optional web search, and Pipecat can consume text through shared-bus or stdin/stdout and then forward it into LLM, TTS, or transport services. Without a verification step, Pipecat may treat Khoj output as authoritative and propagate errors downstream.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Khoj output as prompt or transcript input
IF no validation step checks Khoj citations or provenance
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pipecat acts on Khoj output
Require source citations for any factual claim
Limit downstream actions to read-only responses
requires-engineering: add schema validation for exchanged messages

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is self-hostable and stores personal notes/documents, while Pipecat commonly sends audio/text to external providers and analytics services. That creates a residency and retention mismatch risk for the same data class, even though no specific certification gap is documented for either agent.
conditions: IF personal notes or conversation text are processed by external Pipecat providers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the transferred data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external Pipecat services
Review provider residency and retention settings
Disable analytics exports for sensitive sessions
requires-engineering: document a DPA and retention policy mapping
